Integrated GIS-Based Multi-Criteria Approach for Seismic Hazard Mapping in the Arabian–Eurasian Convergence Zone

📅 2026-08-19 ✍️ Kaifi Chomani, Shaki Pshdari, Rajab Ali et al. (Scientific Reports) 🏷️ GIS, seismic hazard mapping, multi-criteria analysis, geospatial, Arabian–Eurasian convergence zone, earthquake, fault lines
🔗 Read the source article →

💡 Quick summary

Researchers have published an integrated GIS-based multi-criteria geospatial approach for seismic hazard mapping in the tectonically active Arabian–Eurasian convergence zone, combining multiple geospatial data layers to produce comprehensive earthquake risk maps.

📌 Key takeaways

  • The study was published in Scientific Reports on August 19, 2026, as an open-access article
  • The research integrates GIS-based multi-criteria analysis with geospatial techniques to map seismic hazards in the Arabian–Eurasian convergence zone
  • The approach combines multiple geospatial data layers — including fault proximity, seismic history, geology, and topography — to produce a comprehensive seismic hazard assessment
  • The methodology provides a reproducible framework applicable to other tectonically active regions worldwide
  • The study received institutional review through Nature's peer-review process, accepted August 13, 2026
